description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of emotional categories in a dataset used for evaluating speaker anonymization on emotional speech, with each slice representing a distinct emotion and its corresponding proportion. The chart is divided into six labeled segments: "Frustration" (25.1%, light blue), "Neutral" (23.1%, dark blue), "Happiness" (14.1%, red), "Sadness" (14.7%, orange), "Anger" (14.9%, yellow), and an unlabeled category represented by a gray segment. The percentages are clearly labeled within each slice, and the segments are arranged in a clockwise order starting from the top. The largest portion is attributed to "Frustration," followed closely by "Neutral," while the remaining emotions are comparatively smaller, with "Happiness" being the smallest labeled category. The gray segment, which lacks a label, appears to represent a small proportion of the total, though its exact value is not specified. The chart effectively visualizes the relative frequency of each emotional state in the dataset.
